result.summary: Manual review of the batch 10 icon assets and provenance files found no concrete defects. Seven SVGs (natsdotio, oracle, postgresql, redis, sqlite, text, valkey) have SHA-256 values that match their sources.json entries. Two things could not be checked from the supplied evidence: the SVG contents, and whether MIT/Apache license texts for the other upstream sources are bundled. I recorded both as limitations and evidence requests, not defects. This is not a canonical CR and does not approve BUILD.
limitations: No obligations were assigned to this batch, so there are no holds/does-not-hold results.

The SVG file contents were not supplied, only byte counts and SHA-256 values. I could not check for scripts or external references, or confirm that the bytes match the upstream files. The seven supplied hashes match their sources.json entries.

sources.json lists icons that are not in this batch (mysql, mariadb, mongodb, memcached, mssql, dynamodb, csv, json, excel, keydb and others). I could not check those files, and I could not check the upstream URLs or commits.

sources.json lists devicons (MIT), gilbarbara/logos (CC0) and Apache-2.0-labelled brand entries. Only the simple-icons CC0 and vscode-icons MIT texts appear in this batch. A devicon MIT notice, a gilbarbara notice or Apache attribution may be in another batch, so I cannot tell whether the bundled attribution is complete.
I did not check packaging inclusion (.vscodeignore, package files) or any code that maps database kinds to these icons, because none was supplied.
I did not check the Content-Security-Policy or webview resource handling for these assets.
evidenceRequests: Directory listing of vscode-plugin/media/datasources/ showing whether a devicon MIT license file and any gilbarbara/logos or Apache attribution/NOTICE file are bundled.
The SVG contents, or an independent hash check of all files against sources.json, to confirm there are no script or external-reference elements.
The code that maps datasource kinds to icon files, and the packaging configuration (.vscodeignore or files list) that includes media/datasources in the VSIX.
